title: Model Directions, Not Words: Mechanistic Topic Models Using Sparse Autoencoders
venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics, vol. 14
subcategory: topic models over sparse-autoencoder features of an LLM
task: Topic modelling with abstract, feature-level topic descriptions and topic steering
problem: Bag-of-words and word-list topics cannot express abstract concepts such as style or tone.
architecture: Mechanistic Topic Models (mLDA, mETM, mBERTopic) replace words with interpretable SAE features of an LLM (GemmaScope 16k SAE, layer 10 of Gemma 2-9B) with descriptions from Neuronpedia; topics become distributions over features and can be turned into steering vectors for controllable generation; 'topic judge' evaluates models by LLM pairwise comparisons aggregated with a Bradley-Terry/Elo model.
llm_or_encoder: Gemma 2-9B with GemmaScope SAEs; GPT-4.1 as judge
key_results: An MTM has the highest Elo in 14 of 16 dataset-representation rows; MTMs beat their word-based counterparts in 42 of 48 pairwise comparisons.
Human and LLM Elo agree strongly (Spearman 0.83 on Wiki and 0.95 on PoemSum with top-feature representations).
strengths: Feature-level topics capture abstract themes (tone, style) beyond word lists, with gains on short and abstract datasets.
Only topic model reported to enable controllable text generation via topic steering.
Proposes an evaluation that works across different vocabularies (words vs features).

limitations.text: Depends on pretrained SAEs and external feature descriptions; SAEs have known weaknesses on downstream tasks.
Not compared with prompting-based LLM topic models such as TopicGPT because of API cost.

notes: K = 50 or 100; hyper-parameters tuned by Bayesian optimisation.
